external_entities.name: sensor node
external_entities.description: A deployed sensor node installed on a customer site that publishes readings and polls for firmware updates.
external_entities.source_excerpt: We have a few thousand sensor nodes installed on customer sites.
external_entities.notes: The nodes are outside our physical control. The fleet uses one pre-shared key rather than a per-device key.

external_entities.name: field technician
external_entities.description: A technician who services sensor nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.notes: The source does not state whether the serial console has authentication.

external_entities.name: fleet operator
external_entities.description: An operator who views telemetry dashboards from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network

processes.name: device gateway
processes.description: An MQTT broker running on GKE that accepts sensor readings and forwards them to Pub/Sub.
processes.source_excerpt: the device gateway, which is an MQTT broker we run on GKE and expose to the internet
processes.notes: Nodes authenticate to the broker with a pre-shared key. The key is per fleet, not per device, and has not been rotated since deployment.

processes.name: telemetry normalizer
processes.description: A Python consumer that picks up readings from Pub/Sub and writes them into the telemetry lake.
processes.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

data_stores.name: device registry
data_stores.description: A Firestore registry used to check a device key and determine which customer a node belongs to.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

data_stores.name: Pub/Sub
data_stores.description: A messaging store onto which the gateway forwards accepted readings for the telemetry normalizer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_stores.name: telemetry lake
data_stores.description: A BigQuery data store containing telemetry, site addresses, and occupancy patterns.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

data_stores.name: Cloud Storage bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket from which sensor nodes poll for firmware images.
data_stores.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image
data_stores.notes: The bucket is public read. The source does not establish whether nodes verify a signature before installing an image.

data_flows.name: publish readings
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway

data_flows.name: look up device
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

data_flows.name: forward readings
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_flows.name: pick up readings
data_flows.source_excerpt: picked up by the telemetry normalizer

data_flows.name: write readings
data_flows.source_excerpt: which writes them into the telemetry lake in BigQuery

data_flows.name: poll firmware
data_flows.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image
data_flows.notes: The bucket is public read because making the nodes authenticate to it was awkward.

data_flows.name: service node
data_flows.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
data_flows.notes: I don't know what authentication that console has, if any.

data_flows.name: look at dashboards
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

trust_boundaries.name: customer site
trust_boundaries.description: A customer-controlled site where sensor nodes are installed and physically accessible to technicians.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: sensor nodes installed on customer sites

trust_boundaries.name: analytics network
trust_boundaries.description: The network in which the telemetry normalizer runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which fleet operators view dashboards.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network

assumptions.assumption: The device gateway presents a non-web interface because it is described as an MQTT broker.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the device gateway as an MQTT broker, which is a non-web service interface.

assumptions.assumption: The customer site is a tenant-controlled trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The sensor nodes are installed on customer sites and are outside our physical control.

assumptions.assumption: The analytics network is a network trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly places the telemetry normalizer in an analytics network.

assumptions.assumption: The corporate network is a network trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly places fleet operators in the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The device registry contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It contains a device key and the customer association for each node.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the lake contains site addresses and occupancy patterns and calls it customer data.
